clue.text: Block request for reversible material

parts.note: to block a river is to dam it
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a fabric that can be worn either way out to be blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a woven fabric whose pattern shows on both faces, so it can be used either side up.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

definitions.meaning: a failing is a fault or flaw
to desert one cause for its opponent

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a flaw and a verb for going over to the enemy.

clue.text: State of bird protecting egg in her home

indicators.note: the bird's name wraps round, shielding what goes inside it

parts.note: the mina (myna) is an Asian starling

indicators.note: the egg is placed inside the bird's home

parts.note: a bird's home is her nest
an egg is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bird guarding an egg in her nest somewhere in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside NEST to make NESOT; 'protecting' splits MINA as MIN...A round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the states of the USA, in the upper Midwest.

clue.text: Smooth talking man with a woman picked up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mr is the title of a man
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A man and a woman get together, perhaps after some flattering chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal or a pick-up line; in this down clue it turns MRAMS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarm is oily, ingratiating flattery, smooth talk meant to win favour.

clue.text: Notices ducks leaving river by double bend

parts.note: the letter S has the shape of a double bend in a road

indicators.note: the river's letter departs from the ducks' name

parts.note: mallards are common wild ducks

explanation.surface: Signs warn of ducks wandering from a river beside an S-bend in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ads are short classified notices in a newspaper offering things for sale or wanted.

clue.text: Stew or a Chinese in club? Some other food

indicators.note: the stewed letters go inside the club

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club

indicators.note: to stew things is to mix them up in a pot, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between a stew or a Chinese meal at the club, or some other dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' rearranges OR A CHINESE to ARONICHEES; 'in' puts that inside MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta dish, a food quite other than a stew or a Chinese takeaway.

clue.text: Objectionable person holding book up — you won't influence him

indicators.note: the louse contains the next piece

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person

indicators.note: in a down clue the book's name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: An unpleasant man clutches a book upside down and cannot be persuaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ACTS to STCA, and 'holding' puts it inside LOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a person or project beyond help, so no effort will change him.

clue.text: Sort of explanation? A slick one no good

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good is to be dropped

parts.note: slick talk is glib
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A smooth excuse that turns out to be worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from GLIB, leaving LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is an account offered to show one was elsewhere, an excuse or explanation.

clue.text: Calm conditions, presumably, at this reference height?

definitions.text: Calm conditions, presumably, at this reference height?

parts.words: Calm conditions, presumably, at this reference height?
parts.note: the datum for measuring altitude is read playfully as the sea being flat in calm weather

explanation.definitionFit: Heights are measured from mean sea level, and a calm sea would literally be level.

clue.text: United's ground trains militia, an idea of the greatest benefit

definitions.text: an idea of the greatest benefit

parts.note: U is short for United in team names

indicators.note: something ground is broken up, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Football club United's stadium is used to drill a citizen army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like United's stadium; it is the past tense of grind, rearranging TRAINS MILITIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilitarianism is the doctrine that actions are right if they produce the greatest good for the greatest number.

clue.text: Terrific enthusiast gets little thanks and endless criticism

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
ta is a short, informal thank you

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: stick is informal for harsh criticism

explanation.surface: A keen supporter is barely thanked and constantly criticised, which is just terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks; 'endless' drops the K of STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic and terrific are both informal words meaning excellent.

clue.text: Star beginning to suffer with eating disorder

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: pica is a craving to eat non-food substances

explanation.surface: A celebrity starts to struggle with an eating problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo.

clue.text: Line given audibly?

parts.note: an actor's prompt is a line spoken aloud, and the word also sounds like a word for a line of people

explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the spoken line that signals the next actor to speak, and it sounds like queue.

clue.text: Pair perform, beset by spite and unprofessionalism

indicators.note: surrounded by, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: malice is spite
to perform is to act

explanation.surface: A double act performs amid nastiness and unprofessional behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts PRACT inside MALICE, split as MAL...ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Malpractice is improper or negligent conduct by a professional, a lack of professionalism.

clue.text: Brief time for force to turn things around

definitions.meaning: in physics, the turning effect of a force about a point

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an instant and, in mechanics, a force's turning effect, as in moment of force.

clue.text: Processes of turning out computer-based equivalents?

parts.note: the prefix e- marks something electronic, as in e-book
versions are equivalent forms of a thing

explanation.surface: Electronic copies are the products of computer work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' looks like producing; it means turning inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eversion is the act of turning an organ or part outwards or inside out.

clue.text: Nerve centre given new currency needs a little more again

annotationWithheld.why: Nerve centre given new currency needs a little more again (7): N + EURO gives NEUR, but no reading of 'needs a little more again' gives the final NE or ONE without stretching
annotationWithheld.clue: Nerve centre given new currency needs a little more again

clue.text: Possible instruction to get from commercial document

parts.note: to order goods is to instruct someone to supply them

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the letters, not the one printed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A form explains how to obtain something from a company.
explanation.definitionFit: An order form is the business paper a customer fills in to request goods.

clue.text: Vehicle to go quickly up under overhead line

definitions.text: Vehicle to go quickly up under overhead line

indicators.note: in a down clue the next piece sits beneath the line written above it

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle for hire

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to race is to go quickly

explanation.surface: A carriage climbs fast hanging from a cable strung overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RACE into ECAR, placed below CAB and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable car is a cabin hauled uphill hanging from an overhead cable.

clue.text: Ham tea served in a very old city

indicators.note: the tea is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
mate is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A ham-and-tea meal served in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat; it means a poor performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an unskilled performer, so an amateur, as in a ham radio operator.

clue.text: Church writings — lots to read, beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter goes to the end of the word

parts.note: a screed is a long piece of writing

explanation.surface: Religious texts make for heavy reading from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves the S of SCREED to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeds are formal statements of Christian belief, such as the Nicene Creed.

clue.text: Lad hiding big belly? Too right

indicators.note: the lad covers what goes inside

parts.note: a son is a lad
a pot is a paunch, as in pot belly

explanation.surface: A boy covers up his paunch, quite rightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British informal for exactly right.

clue.text: Group terribly austere beginning to shun those who aren't

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: badly, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A severe group starting to avoid people who are not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges AUSTERE into USEATER. 'those who aren't' means people who are not austere.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters, from Homer, are people given up to idle luxury, the opposite of austere.

clue.text: Article reduced — "steal" for pound

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A news article is shortened, swapping theft for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound and to throb both mean to beat heavily, as a heart does.

clue.text: Country girl wants daughter rather than son

indicators.note: one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: Susan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wants a daughter, not a son.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the second S of SUSAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: On radio, cover strike

indicators.note: broadcast, so heard, not seen

parts.note: to wrap is to cover

explanation.surface: A broadcast about insurance against industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap is a sharp blow or knock, a strike.

clue.text: Copper has curtailed disturbance — it's an odd thing

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: its tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: a riot is a disturbance

explanation.surface: A police officer has cut short a riot, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal. 'curtailed' drops the T of RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a curiosity, an unusual collectable object.

clue.text: Cox's words to engage crew that's turned the wrong way

indicators.note: the call holds the crew inside it

parts.note: a cox calls the rowing rhythm, in and out
a side is a team or crew

explanation.surface: The cox's commands set a crew going, but the boat has turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage' puts SIDE inside IN OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside out describes something reversed so its inner surface faces outwards.

clue.text: Cellular particle in one part of the body about to circulate

indicators.note: to go round, so the word wraps the others

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
the bosom is the chest

explanation.surface: A particle in a body part is about to be carried round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circulate' puts I and BOSOM inside RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribosome is a tiny particle in a cell where proteins are made.

clue.text: It casts a shadow to some extent having no money

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being broke partly overshadows things.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnomon is the pointer on a sundial whose shadow shows the time.
